A composite of perception-based surveys (WGI 2025 revision, history recalculated back to 1996), roughly -2.5 (weak) to +2.5 (strong). The World Bank defines political stability as perceptions of the likelihood of politically motivated violence, including civil unrest and terrorism. Annual. The World Bank publishes 90 percent confidence intervals, which are not used here: single-year differences between countries can lie within them. The cut-offs 0.0 and -1.0 are project-defined conventions chosen on the conventional scale and have not been re-checked against the revised series.
This level for Taiwan does not measure cross-strait tension or military activity: it uses only the absence of a UCDP-recorded state-based armed conflict and the WGI perception estimate.
The level reflects measured violence and instability perceptions only, not interstate tension.
